paper.title_en: Configuration-constrained multiquasiparticle states in <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>150</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>152</mn></mrow></math> Fm–Sg isotones
paper.abstract_en: Configuration-constrained potential-energy-surface calculations are performed for two- and four-quasiparticle states in the eight even-even <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>150</mn></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>152</mn></mrow></math> Fm–Sg isotones using a deformed Woods-Saxon potential, Lipkin-Nogami pairing, and Strutinsky macroscopic-microscopic energies. Vacuum and blocked surfaces are minimized independently over deformations <math><mrow><mo>{</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo>}</mo></mrow></math>. Orbital-overlap tracing preserves the blocked Nilsson configurations near avoided crossings, while component decompositions and species-dependent pairing-gap reductions provide complementary validation. Across the two isotonic chains, the neutron <math><msup><mn>7</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></math> and <math><msup><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></math> excitations increase from <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>150</mn></mrow></math> to <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>152</mn></mrow></math>, whereas the neutron <math><msup><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math> sequence decreases. The proton <math><msup><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></math> sequence develops a pronounced minimum near Rf, with calculated energies of 1.120 and 1.123 MeV in <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rf</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>254</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rf</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>256</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. All minima remain strongly deformed, with <math><mrow><mn>0.231</mn><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.251</mn></mrow></math>, small <math><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math>, and predominantly negative, configuration-dependent <math><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></math>. Blocking produces only small shape polarization, although the <math><msubsup><mn>16</mn><mn>613</mn><mo>+</mo></msubsup></math> and <math><msubsup><mn>16</mn><mn>624</mn><mo>+</mo></msubsup></math> families show slightly different nonaxial responses. In <math><mmultiscripts><mi>No</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>254</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, the <math><msup><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math> bandhead is reproduced within 30 keV, whereas the neutron <math><msup><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math> state is underestimated by 0.534 MeV despite retaining the intended <math><mrow><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>734</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>725</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math> orbital character. The sensitivity to the neutron pairing strength is examined: its 10% increase reproduces the empirical pairing indicator but leaves the <math><msup><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math> energy 0.346 MeV below experiment, implicating the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>152</mn></mrow></math> single-particle spacing and possibly residual correlations. The calculated <math><msubsup><mn>16</mn><mn>613</mn><mo>+</mo></msubsup></math> state at 2.737 MeV lies closer to the experimental 2.933-MeV <math><msup><mn>16</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math> state than the <math><msubsup><mn>16</mn><mn>624</mn><mo>+</mo></msubsup></math> solution at 3.749 MeV, favoring the <math><mrow><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>613</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math> configuration at the uncorrected mean-field level.
